title: Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range
objective: I can find the range and the interquartile range of a data set and use them to describe how spread out the data is.
model: ordered data and its box plot: range = whisker end to whisker end, IQR = length of the box

widgets.component: Warm-up on box plot parts and a five-number summary
widgets.root: Matches the lesson's warm-up; five-number summary of 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 14 = 2, 5, 8, 11, 14 verified.

widgets.component: Range, IQR, which measure uses the middle half, same-median compare, IQR-larger-than-range error
widgets.root: Keys verified; the err item (IQR = 58 + 42 = 100) catches add-instead-of-subtract and the impossible 'IQR > range'.

widgets.component: Range and IQR from a box plot, 20-score match, salary compare, range overreads
widgets.root: Rechecked the 20 scores: Q1 75.5, median 83.5, Q3 88, range 26, IQR 12.5; the 15-18-20-22-25-60 err gives IQR 7.

widgets.component: Shape (skewed left), center + spread + shape, equal medians do not mean equal shape
widgets.root: The lesson's objective is range and IQR; these three items assess distribution shape, which is lesson 2-2's skill, and 3.6's key also computes a mean (720 ÷ 9). 3.5 says 'Class A's test scores are shown on a dot plot' but no dot plot is drawn.
widgets.replacement: Replace with three box-plot items on the lesson's Class A / Class B plots: (a) 'Which class has the larger range? Which has the larger IQR?', (b) 'Class B's range is smaller by 8 but its IQR is smaller by 5: which measure is more affected by Class A's low score of 62?', (c) 'A new score of 100 is added to Class B: which of range or IQR changes more?' Use `box` figures.

widgets.component: Range of a sorted list; Q1 or IQR with the odd-count rule; range and IQR from data or a box plot
widgets.root: Sampled 120 seeds per level: L1 range from an ordered list, L2 Q1 / IQR with the stated rule, L3 both from data or a figure. The rule text is in the stem, so the odd-count trap is taught, not guessed.

widgets.component: Build the chart: sort, mark five numbers, answer what fraction of the data is inside the box
widgets.root: The L2 build ends with 'What fraction of the data is inside the box?' (lesson 2-4's idea) and never asks for the range or IQR; the typed-IQR step only starts at L3.
widgets.replacement: Make the final step at every level a typed pair: 'range = ___ and IQR = ___', graded against max − min and Q3 − Q1, with named feedback for 'range typed in the IQR box' and 'median typed as Q1'. Move the 'fraction in the box' question to 2-4.

widgets.component: 'Range of Class A', 'IQR of Class B', 'what do the smaller range and IQR tell you about Class B'
widgets.root: No data: Class A (62, 74, 81, 87, 90) and Class B (70, 76, 81, 84, 90) exist only in the lesson's Connect scenario and its two box plots, which the studio dropped.
widgets.replacement: Attach the two Connect figures as one `box` viz: plots Class A {min 62, q1 74, med 81, q3 87, max 90} and Class B {min 70, q1 76, med 81, q3 84, max 90}, scale 60–95 step 5, label 'Math test score'. Keys stay 28, 8, 'less spread out'.

widgets.component: IQR meaning, which measure an extreme value changes, IQR of six watering times
widgets.root: Keys verified (16; range changes most; lower half 3.5, 5, 6 gives 5 and upper 7.5, 9, 10 gives 9 so IQR 4).

widgets.component: IQR/Q1 from data, range and IQR from a plot, compare two score lists
widgets.root: Compared the Hawk/Owl L4 lists by hand (Hawk IQR 2, range 39; Owl IQR 11, range 18) against the generated key.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 items 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 (err, tbl, mc with box figure, tbl, num)
widgets.component: Same-median error, sunflower table, tomato beds, bean pod outlier before / after, maximum from range
widgets.root: Rechecked 11 sunflowers (range 41, Q1 48, Q3 66, IQR 18); 8 pods vs 9 with 45 (range 9 to 33, IQR 4 to 5.5); Bed A range 40 IQR 16 vs Bed B 80 and 10.

widgets.component: Predict how each class's IQR changes when one 80 is added
widgets.root: The class sizes and score lists are not given, so the stated range and IQR cannot determine whether an added 80 raises, lowers or leaves the IQR; the model answer asserts 'stays the same or shrinks' without data and the keyword grader accepts any fluent paragraph.
widgets.replacement: Give the 8 scores of a small class (e.g. 62, 70, 74, 78, 81, 84, 87, 90), have the student compute range and IQR before and after adding 80 by filling a 2 x 2 table (range, IQR; before, after), then write one sentence saying which measure moved and why.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 items 1-2 (act:chartbuild mode box, L3-L4), item 3 (sort)
widgets.component: Build the chart with a typed IQR; sort descriptions to range / IQR / both
widgets.root: Typed IQR is graded against Q3 − Q1 and the 'typed the range' slip is named; the sort separates 'extremes' from 'middle half'.

widgets.component: Range / IQR error analysis, typical vs extreme snail, ranges and IQRs of tomato plants and packets, 'can IQR exceed range', minimum from range
widgets.root: Checked each: snail lengths 12-48 (range 36, IQR 2.5); Packet X IQR 20 vs Y 6; IQR can never exceed range; 45 − 28 = 17.
